# Operations

- OPS-007 (must): Avoid blocking calls; make hot code paths asynchronous, and call data access, I/O and long-running operations APIs asynchronously if an asynchronous API is available; avoid reading large request bodies or response bodies into memory; don't create and dispose of HttpClient instances directly, and use HttpClientFactory to retrieve them (OPS-008 names the lifetime options); don't use HttpContext after the request is complete, and don't access it from multiple threads. For high-performance logging scenarios in .NET 6 and later, use LoggerMessageAttribute with compile-time source generation.
- OPS-008 (should): For HttpClient lifetime, you should use either long-lived clients with PooledConnectionLifetime set or short-lived clients created by IHttpClientFactory; what matters is that clients aren't created and disposed with each request. If an app requires cookies, it's recommended to avoid IHttpClientFactory: pooling the HttpMessageHandler instances results in sharing of CookieContainer objects. When adding resilience, you should only add one resilience handler and avoid stacking handlers.
- OPS-011 (must): Every log call in an app goes through a generated, LoggerMessage-based method, not a logger extension method such as LogInformation.
